subject.title: fix(backup): close archive stream before retry cleanup

question: Should OpenClaw still land the stream-ownership hardening after https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101449, or treat the merged retry-temp isolation as sufficient?
rationale: Current main already fixed the central retry cascade by changing temp archive paths, but this PR addresses a distinct node-tar output-writer lifetime concern that automation should not discard or force through without maintainer intent.

options.title: Rebase and land narrowed hardening
options.body: Keep the pipeline-owned archive writer, integrate it with current-main retry-temp isolation, and fix the changelog/test blockers before merge.

options.title: Close as superseded
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101449 as sufficient for the user-visible retry failure and close this branch without carrying the extra stream-lifecycle change.

recommendation.title: Rebase and land narrowed hardening
recommendation.body: Keep the pipeline-owned archive writer, integrate it with current-main retry-temp isolation, and fix the changelog/test blockers before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the current PR steward and also has recent backup-area history, making him the clearest owner for whether this replacement should still land.
